scope: Living requirements catalogue, not a parity or readiness claim

items.name: Organization workspaces
items.acceptance: Two companies cannot read each other's project records
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). No account service is selected and authentication ships disabled by default, so this row cannot be assessed. There is no organisation or tenant model; project records are local to one profile.

items.name: Individual sign-in and sign-out
items.acceptance: Sign-out removes access and cached private views
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). A Better Auth server with federated providers exists but ships disabled, email and password sign-in is switched off in code and no sign-in or sign-out forms are built (`src/lib/auth/`). With authentication off the app resolves a development identity, so sign-out behaviour cannot be assessed.

items.name: Staff invitations
items.acceptance: An accepted invitation grants only the invited role
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). No account service is selected and authentication ships disabled by default, so this row cannot be assessed. There is no invitation model.

items.name: Project roles
items.acceptance: Viewer cannot edit; estimator cannot approve engineering
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). No account service is selected and authentication ships disabled by default, so this row cannot be assessed. There is no project role model. The assistant permission mode governs tool execution, not user roles, and must not be read as satisfying this row.

items.name: Document and field permissions
items.acceptance: Restricted rates remain hidden in screens and exports
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). No account service is selected and authentication ships disabled by default, so this row cannot be assessed. There is no field-level permission, so restricted rates cannot be hidden in screens or exports.

items.name: External guest access
items.acceptance: Guest sees only explicitly shared packages
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). No account service is selected and authentication ships disabled by default, so this row cannot be assessed. There is no guest access or shared package.

items.name: Access revocation
items.acceptance: Previously valid links and sessions lose access when revoked
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). No account service is selected and authentication ships disabled by default, so this row cannot be assessed. There is no session or link revocation.

items.name: Multi-factor and enterprise identity
items.acceptance: Enforced identity policy survives account recovery
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). Federated sign-in through a broker is scaffolded for two providers, but multi-factor policy and account recovery are not implemented and authentication is disabled by default (`src/lib/auth/providers.ts`).

items.name: Staff directory and teams
items.acceptance: Reassignment preserves historical authorship
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). No account service is selected and authentication ships disabled by default, so this row cannot be assessed. There is no staff directory, so authorship cannot survive reassignment.

items.name: Audit trail
items.acceptance: Actor, time, action and affected revision are recorded
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Assistant actions are journalled with work packets and raw task events, and takeoff evidence approval records a named reviewer with a timestamp (`src/studio/assistant/workPacketStore.ts`; SC-12 journey approved evidence for a named person). Remaining: there is no application-wide audit trail of actor, time, action and affected revision, and with no accounts the actor is not an authenticated identity.

items.name: Account recovery and offboarding
items.acceptance: Removed staff cannot retain active organization access
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). No account service is selected and authentication ships disabled by default, so this row cannot be assessed. There is no offboarding path.

items.name: Regional settings
items.acceptance: Units, currency, date and timezone are explicit per project
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Units are fixed to millimetres by schema and currency is ISO-4217 validated per price book with an effective date and tax basis (`src/studio/architect/model.ts`, `priceBooks.ts`). Remaining: regional settings are not explicit or editable per project, and date and timezone handling is not declared.

items.name: Custom fields and classifications
items.acceptance: Required fields validate and survive export/import
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There are no user-defined custom fields or classifications, so validation and survival through export and import cannot be assessed.

items.name: Organization templates
items.acceptance: Template revisions do not silently alter existing projects
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There are no organisation templates, so no template revision can alter an existing project. This is blocked behind the same missing account and organisation model as the rest of category A.

items.name: Create and name projects
items.acceptance: Unique IDs survive duplicate display names
items.assessmentText: State: verified (reviewed by Codex 2026-09-11, built browser on DANS1). The Project library creates and reopens two identically named projects with distinct IDs. Code: src/studio/ProjectLibrary.tsx, src/studio/projectRegistry.ts. Exact patch, 34 tests, dev/production journeys, fixture/build hashes and inspected desktop/tablet screenshots: proof/growth/2026-09-11-project-library/README.md. No installed/native platform claim.

items.name: Automatic save feedback
items.acceptance: Saved appears only after durable storage succeeds
items.assessmentText: State: partial. Re-verified in development 2026-09-08 for the main project record: "saved · revision N" appears only after a readback-verified write; an injected quota failure shows "not confirmed saved" with a retry that succeeds once storage recovers. Code/proof: [SC-02 protected saves](proof/growth/2026-09-08-az3-protected-saves/README.md), [walkthrough](walkthrough.md). Remaining: per-module records, production/native build.

items.name: Save As and duplicate
items.acceptance: Copy gets new identity without sharing mutable records
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no Save As or duplicate action. The registry can shelve and switch projects but does not fork one into a new identity with independent mutable records.

items.name: Reopen recent projects
items.acceptance: Latest saved revision and source sheets return after restart
items.assessmentText: State: partial (updated 2026-09-11). Project library lists saved projects and reopens the exact project ID, revision 2 and original drawing after page reload, archive and restore. Code: src/studio/ProjectLibrary.tsx. Proof: proof/growth/2026-09-11-project-library/README.md. Remaining: full browser-process/installed-app restart with the same source fixture; a page reload is not that test.

items.name: Offline local storage
items.acceptance: Airplane-mode restart restores drawings and attached originals
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Storage is local first: drawings, price books and attached originals persist in browser storage and IndexedDB with no network dependency, and a 9.3 MB backup was captured and read back in a live journey (SC-10). Remaining: an airplane-mode restart has not been executed as a declared scenario.

items.name: Cross-device project storage
items.acceptance: Authorized second device opens the same confirmed revision
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no cross-device storage. Persistence is local to one browser profile or one desktop install, and no account service is selected.

items.name: Archive and restore projects
items.acceptance: Archived jobs leave the active list and restore intact
items.assessmentText: State: verified (reviewed by Codex 2026-09-11, built browser on DANS1). Archive hides inactive projects and assistant tabs; restore retains the original project ID, revision, source records and SHA-256-verified drawing bytes. Only the registry marker changes; stored project data is preserved. Current, unreadable and stale targets are refused. Code: src/studio/projectArchive.ts, src/studio/ProjectLibrary.tsx, src/studio/assistant/projectSwitch.ts. Exact diff, executed failure-path tests and inspected desktop/tablet proof: proof/growth/2026-09-11-project-library/README.md. Portable backup restoration remains B-09; installed/native acceptance is separate.

items.name: Recycle bin
items.acceptance: Accidental removal is recoverable with links and history intact
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no recycle bin. Source-page archive and recover is the nearest behaviour and is assessed under D-04 and D-05.

items.name: Portable complete backup
items.acceptance: Restore on a clean profile includes sources, models, rates and evidence
items.assessmentText: State: partial (reviewed 2026-09-11). V2 restoration now runs before editor hydration under an exclusive workspace lease, with an immutable incoming package, recovery copy, validated before/after journal, non-overwriting originals and active job switched last. A transferred package restores an exact project revision and original SVG SHA-256 in a fresh browser context. Code: src/studio/workspaceRestoreStorage.ts, src/studio/workspaceRestorePlan.ts, src/studio/WorkspaceStartup.tsx. Proof: proof/growth/2026-09-11-restore/README.md. Remaining: complete sources/models/rates/evidence fixture coverage, excluded assistant/runtime/model-preference context, installed/native and clean-machine acceptance.

items.name: Backup integrity preview
items.acceptance: Corrupt or missing assets block replacement before any write
items.assessmentText: State: verified (reviewed by Codex 2026-09-11, built browser on DANS1). Packages, original identities and destination fingerprints are revalidated before staging and again before protected application. Corrupt originals introduced after review refuse the real restore action, preserve the active record and retain conflicting source bytes. Missing/corrupt package assets and source collisions are also covered by executed tests. Code: src/studio/backupRestorePreflight.ts, src/studio/workspaceRestoreStorage.ts, src/studio/BackupRestoreReview.tsx. Exact patch, 45 tests, production browser receipts and inspected screenshots: proof/growth/2026-09-11-restore/README.md. Native acceptance and full-project coverage remain separate.

items.name: Crash and interrupted-write recovery
items.acceptance: Last confirmed snapshot survives forced termination
items.assessmentText: State: partial (reviewed 2026-09-11). Backup restore now journals before-images and recovers prepared/writing phases before editor hydration; ambiguous save acknowledgements stop writes and replay the durable phase on reload. Injected module failures and simulated persisted interruption pass, including browser rollback and damaged-journal refusal. Code: src/studio/workspaceRestore.ts, src/studio/WorkspaceStartup.tsx. Proof: proof/growth/2026-09-11-restore/README.md. Remaining: actual forced process termination mid-write, mixed-version windows and native recovery drills are not proved.

items.name: Concurrent edit protection
items.acceptance: Stale writer cannot silently overwrite a newer revision
items.assessmentText: State: partial. Main project record protected in development 2026-09-08: compare-and-swap against the last loaded/written bytes refuses a stale write and leaves the newer stored revision byte-identical; a cross-window storage event pauses saving with a "newer revision exists" notice offering reload and a download of the unsaved revision; reload adopts the newer revision. 49 focused tests, same-window, two-tab and reload-failure Fast CDP proof, three independent verifiers not refuted. Code/proof: [SC-02 protected saves](proof/growth/2026-09-08-az3-protected-saves/README.md). Remaining: per-module records (BOM, inventory, architecture, price books, sheet metadata), Web Lock lease, production/native build.

items.name: Storage failure recovery
items.acceptance: Full disk/quota error preserves previous data and supports retry
items.assessmentText: State: partial. Main project record verified in development 2026-09-08: quota throw and silent-write failures keep the previously stored bytes byte-identical and the in-memory edit; an explicit retry persists it (store test plus tablet 1024x768 Fast CDP proof). Code/proof: [SC-02 protected saves](proof/growth/2026-09-08-az3-protected-saves/README.md). Remaining: IndexedDB originals/materials and per-module records, production/native build.

items.name: Migration and retention
items.acceptance: Older supported backups upgrade with a reversible audit record
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). A supported legacy schema migrates forward and an unsupported one fails closed with the original bytes preserved, asserted by test (`src/studio/persistence.ts`). Remaining: migration is not reversible and produces no audit record, which is the substance of this row.

items.name: Lines, polylines, arcs and circles
items.acceptance: Exact coordinates survive save and CAD exchange
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Lines, arcs and circles are authored entities and survive a hash-bound DXF round trip that restores stable IDs exactly (`src/studio/architect/model.ts`, `exchange.ts`; `architect.test.ts` "DXF parametric round trip preserves stable IDs"). A general open polyline entity does not exist: an imported LWPOLYLINE is exploded into separate lines. Remaining: a polyline entity, and coordinate survival through DWG and IFC rather than DXF alone.

items.name: Splines and curves
items.acceptance: Control points and curve tolerance survive supported exchanges
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). No spline or NURBS entity exists in the model schema. Curved geometry is limited to circles and arcs. There is nothing to assess until a curve type is authored.

items.name: Object snaps and tracking
items.acceptance: Endpoint, midpoint, perpendicular and intersection picks are correct
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Seven snap kinds are computed geometrically and each is asserted independently, including line-circle and circle-circle intersections and a tangent at an irrational point (`src/studio/architect/precision.ts` snapPoint; `architect.test.ts` "snap candidates resolve endpoint, midpoint, intersection, perpendicular, extension, centre and tangent"; 72 tests logged 2026-09-10). Remaining: no inspected screenshot of live cursor snapping at the declared viewports, so the row stays partial under the tick rule.

items.name: Numeric and relative entry
items.acceptance: Typed distance/angle yields the expected measured geometry
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Typed length with ortho and polar angle stepping resolves to the exact constrained distance (`src/studio/architect/precision.ts` constrainPoint, asserted at 4500 mm on a 30 degree polar step). Remaining: typed angle and absolute or relative coordinate entry are not implemented, and there is no visual proof.

items.name: Coordinate systems and origins
items.acceptance: Local and project origins transform without drift
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). A single global millimetre space with level elevations is implemented. There is no user coordinate system, origin relocation or rotated working plane, so the row cannot be assessed.

items.name: Layers and visibility
items.acceptance: Hidden, locked and isolated layers retain correct entity membership
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). No CAD drafting layer exists. The model field named layers is a wall assembly material layer, not a visibility or lock container, and DXF export synthesises layer names from levels. Recorded explicitly because the field name invites a false positive.

items.name: Selection and properties
items.acceptance: Window/crossing selection and batch edits affect intended objects only
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). Selection is a single entity id. Window and crossing selection, multi-select and batch property edits are not implemented.

items.name: Move, rotate, scale and copy
items.acceptance: Transform and undo preserve dimensions and IDs
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). Move, rotate, scale, copy and array are not implemented as transforms. Offset and mirror each derive one copy, which does not satisfy this row.

items.name: Offset, trim, extend and fillet
items.acceptance: Edge cases retain valid connected geometry
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Offset, mirror, trim, extend and a tangential fillet are real solvers with asserted results and explicit edge-case refusals: a radius too large for its segments, parallel segments that cannot meet, and an intersection already inside the segment are each rejected with a stated reason (`src/studio/architect/precision.ts`; `architect.test.ts` "precision exact length, mirror, offset, trim, extend and tangential fillet"). Remaining: no inspected screenshot, and connected-geometry survival is proven per operation rather than across a drawing session.

items.name: Blocks and reusable symbols
items.acceptance: Definition update changes intended instances without broken attributes
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). No block, symbol or instance definition exists.

items.name: Constraints and parameters
items.acceptance: Driving dimension regenerates dependent geometry consistently
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). No geometric or dimensional constraint solver exists. Wall-hosted dimensions report geometry; they do not drive it.

items.name: Dimensions, leaders and text
items.acceptance: Annotation values update and plot legibly at scale
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Wall-hosted dimensions are associative: moving a wall end from 4000 to 5000 mm regenerates the annotation text, and plan, elevation and section views regenerate with it (`src/studio/architect/drawing.ts`; `architect.test.ts` "plan, elevations, sections and associative dimensions regenerate after editing"). Remaining: free-standing linear, aligned, angular and radial dimensions, leaders and user-placed text do not exist, and plotted legibility at scale is unproven.

items.name: Hatches, lineweights and plot styles
items.acceptance: Screen and exported output agree on declared styles
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Hatching is genuine scanline geometry with ring containment and hole exclusion across five patterns, and per-primitive widths are emitted for plan, elevation and section output (`src/studio/architect/drawing.ts` hatchLines). Remaining: no user control of lineweight, colour or plot style, and no proof that screen and exported PDF agree on declared styles.

items.name: Undo, redo and transaction history
items.acceptance: One user operation undoes atomically without losing active context
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Undo and redo form a two-stack history capped at 60 steps with redo invalidated on a new edit, bound to Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y, and one architect operation is one transaction (`src/studio/architect/ArchitectWorkspace.tsx`). The assistant undo path is separately proven in the SC-08 journeys. Remaining: history is cleared on project load, so undo does not survive a reopen, and no inspected screenshot covers the keyboard path.

items.name: Multi-file and multi-page import
items.acceptance: PDFs with different page sizes preserve every original page
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Multi-page PDF import stores each page with its own identity and dimensions, and a 13-page Redburn set was imported and retained through native runs (SC-10, SC-13). Remaining: a fixture with deliberately mixed page sizes has not been asserted page by page.

items.name: Sheet names and numbers
items.acceptance: Rename changes labels without breaking evidence references
items.assessmentText: State: partial — verified in development 2026-09-08 for source sheets: rename changes only the page label/discipline; calibrations, traces, items, annotations and saved views stay keyed by original page index and byte-identical; the new name shows in the register, heading and navigation after reload. Fixture Redburn BR250157 (SHA-256 b57956f76b5dc893ac2b28a021f3f92e345807e326d6b1f8313e373f9145ad38, 13 pages); 37 focused tests; three verifiers not refuted. Code/proof: [SC-03 sheets](proof/growth/2026-09-08-az3-sheets/README.md). Remaining: authored architectural sheets, production/native build.

items.name: Add and duplicate drawing sheets
items.acceptance: New sheet receives an independent identity and layout
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Authored sheets can be added, duplicated, renamed, reordered, archived and recovered, each with an independent identity and layout, and duplication does not share viewport records (`src/studio/architect/authoredSheetSet.ts`, tests pass 2026-09-10). Remaining: no inspected screenshot of the authored sheet lifecycle at the declared viewports.

items.name: Remove with impact preview
items.acceptance: Review lists dependent takeoffs, links and viewports before removal
items.assessmentText: State: partial — verified in development 2026-09-08 for source-page archive (the product's removal): the review lists calibrations, measured traces, located items, annotations, linked photos and, newly, saved views for that page, and storage stays unchanged until confirmation. Code/proof: [SC-03 sheets](proof/growth/2026-09-08-az3-sheets/README.md). Remaining: whole-source removal, SHA-bound construction takeoff registers (not page-scoped, so not counted), production/native build.

items.name: Restore removed sheets
items.acceptance: Restored sheet recovers annotations, scale and original ordering
items.assessmentText: State: partial — verified in development 2026-09-08 as archive → recover: the page returns to its original managed slot with identical metadata, its locked scale and a real sketch annotation byte-identical after recover and reload (unit test with job evidence after archive and recover; browser assertions on 13 calibrations and the annotation at every step). Code/proof: [SC-03 sheets](proof/growth/2026-09-08-az3-sheets/README.md). Remaining: authored sheets, production/native build.

items.name: Reorder and group sheets
items.acceptance: Discipline groups and order persist after restart and export
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Verified in the 2026-09-07 acceptance addendum in this file for source-sheet discipline groups, persistent managed order and an actual ordered-register download, retaining every original page identity through reload in browser and Windows-native runs. Remaining: the export is a JSON register, and authored multi-sheet publishing and reordering the source PDF itself are outside that acceptance.

items.name: Title blocks and templates
items.acceptance: Project metadata updates linked fields without clipping
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no title block or template system, so project metadata cannot update linked fields.

items.name: Viewports and per-view scale
items.acceptance: Independent scales measure correctly in exported PDF
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). A sheet carries up to twelve viewports with independent view, level, scale and position, and resizing the paper refits frames without altering viewport scales (`src/studio/architect/authoredSheetSet.ts`). Export is real vector PDF (`sheets.ts`). Remaining: measuring an exported PDF at each declared viewport scale has not been executed.

items.name: Drawing revisions and supersession
items.acceptance: Old revision remains retrievable and visibly superseded
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). Drawing revisions and supersession do not exist. The project carries a revision counter, but old drawing revisions are not retrievable or visibly superseded.

items.name: Revision overlay and slip-sheeting
items.acceptance: Added/deleted geometry is inspectable with alignment controls
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no revision overlay or slip-sheeting, so added and deleted geometry cannot be inspected between issues.

items.name: OCR and sheet indexing
items.acceptance: Suggested names are reviewable and uncertainty is visible
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no OCR or automatic sheet indexing, and therefore no suggested names or visible uncertainty.

items.name: Cross-sheet references and hyperlinks
items.acceptance: Detail callout opens the intended sheet revision
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). Cross-sheet references and detail callouts are not implemented.

items.name: Batch printing and issue sets
items.acceptance: Selected sheets export in reviewed order with an issue register
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no batch printing or issue set. Single-sheet PDF export exists and is assessed under D-08.

items.name: Bookmarks and saved views
items.acceptance: Personal navigation restores the correct page and viewport
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Verified in the 2026-09-07 acceptance addendum in this file for local original-page, zoom and source-relative-centre bookmarks, with pan, zoom, page switching, viewport restoration, resize, reload, removal and failed-write preservation passing, and a tablet sub-check at both declared orientations. Remaining: saved views are local project metadata, with no account synchronisation or sharing.

items.name: Pricing workbook import
items.acceptance: XLSX/CSV sheets preview without executing spreadsheet formulas
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Verified in the 2026-09-07 acceptance addendum in this file for bounded XLSX and CSV preview with no spreadsheet formula execution: a mapped formula is refused despite a cached value, malformed input is preserved, and reload passes in the declared browser and Windows scenarios (`src/studio/priceWorkbook.ts`). Remaining: a 2 MiB source and 20 MiB expanded archive limit, no XLS, XLSM or encrypted files, and the rates used were QA fixtures rather than supplier quotations.

items.name: Column and worksheet mapping
items.acceptance: SKU, description, unit and rate map with row-level errors
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Verified in the 2026-09-07 acceptance addendum in this file for worksheet and heading selection and SKU, description, unit and rate mapping with row and cell errors, where explicit review precedes saving and the source hash, selected worksheet and physical rows survive reload (`src/studio/priceBooks.ts`). Remaining: no inferred currency or unit conversion, and the original workbook bytes are not embedded in backups.

items.name: Named price books and revisions
items.acceptance: Supplier revisions coexist and old estimates remain reproducible
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Price books are append-only and revisioned so supplier revisions coexist and an earlier revision remains readable, with archive supported and a live CSV import creating a named book at library revision 1 (`src/studio/priceBooks.ts`; SC-12 journey). Remaining: reproducing an old estimate against its original revision has not been executed.

items.name: Currency, tax and effective dates
items.acceptance: Mixed currencies never total without a reviewed conversion
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Currency is ISO-4217 validated and totals are grouped by currency, tax basis and decimal places and summed in integer minor units, so mixed currencies never silently total, and an effective date and tax basis are carried per book (`src/studio/priceBooks.ts`). Remaining: there is no reviewed conversion path, so mixed currencies are separated rather than converted.

items.name: Unit and pack normalization
items.acceptance: Each/metre/square-metre/pack conversion shows its dimensional basis
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). Unit is free text carried through from the source workbook. There is no unit or pack normalisation and no dimensional basis display, so the row cannot be assessed.

items.name: Apply and remove a price book
items.acceptance: Impact preview preserves manual overrides and supports undo
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). A price book cannot be applied to measured quantities or removed from them. Worksheet lines can be priced individually, and the quantity bridge returns an explicit unavailable status (`src/studio/crmBridge.ts`).

items.name: Supplier quote comparison
items.acceptance: Equal specifications compare landed cost and exclusions
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). Supplier quote comparison with landed cost and exclusions is not implemented.

items.name: Material, labour and plant build-ups
items.acceptance: Assembly rate reconciles to separately editable components
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no material, labour and plant build-up. Wall layers carry a single rate with density and waste, which is assessed under T-07 and T-11.

items.name: Waste, yield and productivity
items.acceptance: Assumptions remain separate from measured net quantities
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Waste is a declared percentage held separately from net measured geometry, so an order quantity never overwrites the measured demand (`src/studio/architect/geometry.ts`). Remaining: yield and productivity assumptions do not exist.

items.name: Discount, margin and contingency
items.acceptance: Formula order is explicit and totals independently reconcile
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). Discount, margin and contingency are not implemented, so there is no formula order to make explicit.

items.name: Tender alternates and scenarios
items.acceptance: Base and options compare without altering the accepted baseline
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). Tender alternates and scenario comparison are not implemented.

items.name: Escalation and exchange rates
items.acceptance: Source and effective date bind each applied factor
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). Escalation and exchange-rate factors are not implemented. An effective date is recorded per price book but binds no applied factor.

items.name: Quote approval and issue
items.acceptance: Issued estimate freezes rates, quantities, exclusions and revision
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no quote approval or issue, so nothing freezes rates, quantities and exclusions. Takeoff evidence approval for a named reviewer is a separate behaviour assessed under Q-10 and V rows.

items.name: Cost-to-complete and variations
items.acceptance: Approved changes reconcile original budget to current forecast
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). Cost-to-complete and variation reconciliation are not implemented.

categories.title: Field work, construction and site delivery

items.name: Offline field packages
items.acceptance: Required drawings and checklists open without connectivity
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no offline field package. The application itself is local-first, which is assessed under B-05, but no drawings-and-checklists package is produced for site use.

items.name: RFIs
items.acceptance: Question links to exact drawing revision and tracks response/closure
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no request-for-information record linked to a drawing revision.

items.name: Submittals and shop drawing review
items.acceptance: Review route, due date and resubmission history persist
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). Submittal and shop drawing review is not implemented.

items.name: DXF import/export
items.acceptance: Independent reader verifies supported geometry, layers and units
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). DXF export and import round-trip a parametric project byte-for-byte when the embedded hash matches, fall back to a warned geometry parse when the file has been edited, reject a file that does not declare units, and warn explicitly that imported vectors are references rather than inferred walls (`src/studio/architect/exchange.ts`; `architect.test.ts`). Remaining: verification is by the application’s own reader, not an independent one, and layer support is limited by the absence of CAD layers (C-06).

items.name: Native Windows DWG exchange
items.acceptance: Binary file opens independently; unsupported objects are disclosed
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). DWG import and export run through a bundled ACadSharp engine with magic-byte validation, a 16 MB cap, cancellation and round-trip verification, and an independent readback verified a 431-entity two-level fixture (`src-tauri/src/cad.rs`). Remaining: Windows desktop only, other platforms return an explicit unavailable result, and the installed-app path is unverified.

items.name: IFC geometry and property exchange
items.acceptance: Declared schema validates with correct object identity
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). DXF export writes a real ASCII drawing with header units, layer and linetype tables and LINE, LWPOLYLINE, CIRCLE, ARC and TEXT entities, and embeds the parametric project as SHA-256-bound chunks so an unmodified file round-trips to an identical project. A tampered file refuses to restore the stale embedded design and falls back to geometry, and a file that does not declare units is rejected (`src/studio/architect/exchange.ts`; `architect.test.ts`). Remaining: no third-party CAD application has opened the exported file as proof.

items.name: BCF issue exchange
items.acceptance: Viewpoint, object references and discussion survive a second application
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). IFC4 export writes a spatial project, site and building hierarchy with deterministic identifiers and semantic void and fill relationships, asserted at three of each plus a material layer set usage (`src/studio/architect/ifc.ts`; `architect.test.ts`). Remaining: IFC import does not exist, and no external IFC viewer or checker has validated the file.

Remaining: column typing on export is not declared, and XLSX is read-only.

items.name: Referenced file management

Remaining: there is no general external-reference manager for linked drawings.

items.name: Scale calibration per sheet
items.acceptance: Known distance measures correctly after rotation and reload
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Per-sheet calibration converts every supported input unit to metres, round-trips points through a rotated, scaled and translated transform, and is stored per page with duplicate page records rejected and version-1 records migrated (`src/studio/calibration.ts`; `calibration.test.ts`). Remaining: measurement after a deliberate sheet rotation and reload is asserted at transform level, not through an inspected UI journey.

items.name: Separate axes and distorted scans
items.acceptance: Calibration records anisotropy or blocks unsupported measurement
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Calibration refuses zero-length points, singular transforms and inconsistent converted distances, and records declared, inferred and manual provenance with conflict detection that is independent of candidate order and requires explicit resolution (`src/studio/calibration.ts` reconcileCalibrationCandidates). Remaining: anisotropic separately scaled axes are not represented, so distorted scans are refused rather than measured.

items.name: Lengths, perimeters and counts
items.acceptance: Totals match independently measured fixture values
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Length, area, count and sketch measurements exist with tracing runs, gates and topology validation (`src/studio/tracing.ts`, `src/studio/store.ts`; tracing suites pass 2026-09-10). The SC-12 journey traced a run at 5.000 m against a locked 5 m calibration. Remaining: totals are not reconciled against an independently measured fixture across a whole sheet set.

items.name: Areas, holes and net deductions
items.acceptance: Openings subtract once and self-intersections are rejected
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Area measurement subtracts openings through real polygon boolean geometry, and the architect model proves an opening removes exact material volume once, a T intersection is a union rather than a sum, and overlapping or duplicate hosted openings are rejected (`src/studio/architect/geometry.ts`; `architect.test.ts`). Remaining: net deduction is proven in the design model, not for user-drawn takeoff polygons with holes on a source sheet.

items.name: Volumes, slopes and elevations
items.acceptance: 3D quantity basis distinguishes projected from actual surface
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Volume carries an explicit basis: the area-depth method names its calibration and every depth evidence id, and results are re-verified against their operands and job revision so a stale snapshot is refused (`src/studio/construction/quantity.ts`). Remaining: projected versus actual sloped surface area is not distinguished, which is the substance of this row.

items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). AI proposals are validated before they touch the design, with bounds, room closure and hosted-door checks and review-time revision binding, so a proposal built against an older revision is refused (`src/studio/architect/layoutAi.ts`; `architect.test.ts`). Remaining: extraction from a source plan does not retain an exact source region or an uncertainty value, which is the substance of this row.

items.name: AI layout/design proposals
items.acceptance: Proposal is separately reviewable before modifying authored design
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Proposals cannot silently modify the authored design: validation runs first, the permission mode governs whether an edit executes, and a refusal is returned to the model as a tool error it can read (`src/studio/assistant/permissions.ts`, `useAssistantChat.ts`; permission suite passes 2026-09-10). Remaining: no side-by-side proposal preview before acceptance.

items.name: Voice and natural-language actions
items.acceptance: Intended edit is understandable and reversible
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Natural-language actions map to real tools with plain-word intents that never expose raw JSON, and every design edit is undoable through the same history as a manual edit; live journeys drew, edited and undid geometry by entity identifier (SC-08, SC-12, SC-15). Remaining: voice input does not conduct an autonomous conversation.

items.name: AI pricing research assistant
items.acceptance: Source evidence accompanies suggested supplier match and rate
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). The assistant can read price books and import a pasted price book with recorded provenance, but it cannot research a supplier rate because the search credential is not configured and no application path exists (P-03, P-08). Blocked on the same dependency.

items.name: Tool permission and secret boundaries
items.acceptance: AI cannot reveal keys or issue unapproved external mutations
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Provider keys are read only inside server modules under `src/lib/*.server.ts` and never reach browser code, and unapproved external mutation is blocked by the permission gate: in ask mode no edit tool runs until the user allows it, and a stop denies the pending prompt (`src/studio/assistant/permissions.ts`, 36 tests pass 2026-09-10). Remaining: no adversarial attempt to extract a key through the model has been executed.

items.name: Usage limits and cost reporting
items.acceptance: Provider usage is capped and reported per operation
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Usage is estimated and reported as a context meter with a hard stop at the declared budget, folding in provider caps on entries, images and request bytes (`src/studio/assistant/contextBudget.ts`). Remaining: per-operation monetary cost is not reported, and the estimate is a client-side approximation rather than provider-reported usage.

items.name: Human review and rejection
items.acceptance: Rejected proposal leaves authoritative design unchanged
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). A denied permission prompt leaves the design unchanged and returns an explicit refusal rather than failing silently, asserted across allow once, allow for this chat, deny and stop (`src/studio/assistant/permissions.ts`). Remaining: rejecting an already-applied change relies on undo rather than a proposal queue.

items.name: Automation provenance
items.acceptance: Prompt/input version, tool and accepted changes are traceable
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Work packets persist the objective, the actions taken and the raw task events, and tool receipts are bound to the design revision they changed (`src/studio/assistant/workPacket.ts`, `workPacketStore.ts`). Remaining: the prompt or manual version in force is not recorded alongside the accepted changes.

items.name: Integration health and retries
items.acceptance: Unavailable service is visible and retry does not duplicate work
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). An unconfigured or failing provider is reported truthfully rather than hidden: the pricing route distinguishes not-configured, 401, 402, 429, timeout, abort, oversized and malformed responses, and single-flight refusal prevents a duplicate in-flight request (`src/lib/pricingResearch.server.ts`). Remaining: there is no automatic retry policy, so retry without duplication is proven only for the refusal path.

items.name: Reproducible build identity

items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Release stages freeze the source, count the collected files, record executable and installer digests, inject and verify a build identity and check for source drift after quality assurance (proof/growth/2026-09-09-az5-release/verification.md; LATEST-VERIFIED-BUILD.md). Remaining: builds run from an uncommitted working tree, so a commit and dirty-diff record is not part of the identity.

items.name: Desktop install and upgrade
items.acceptance: Upgrade retains real user profile and compatible project data
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). No build has been installed over the normal application. Every verified package runs from an isolated profile and the register must not imply an upgrade path was tested.

items.name: Offline cold start
items.acceptance: Installed app opens source and design without development services
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). The packaged Windows application starts and completes journeys from an isolated profile without development services, including retained sheets, price books and saved views (SC-11, SC-13 native runs). Remaining: cold start is proven for the packaged executable, not for an installed application.

items.name: Web production parity
items.acceptance: Built site completes the same declared workflows as development
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Each release runs the same declared journeys against the built site and the native application, most recently 40 runs and 765 commands across both for build 8e14ac427997. Remaining: parity is asserted for the declared journeys only, with rendering web-only and the native refusal documented.

items.name: Dependency and license inventory
items.acceptance: Bundled components carry required notices and versions
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no dependency and licence inventory with required notices. A bundled third-party CAD engine and a CC0 asset are recorded individually in their slices, which does not satisfy this row.

items.name: Security and tenant isolation
items.acceptance: Adversarial access tests cannot cross project permissions
items.assessmentText: State: dependency-blocked (assessed 2026-09-10). There are no tenants or permissions to cross. Provider keys are confined to server modules (X-10), but adversarial access testing has no boundary to attack until accounts exist.

items.name: Backup/restore disaster drill
items.acceptance: Clean machine restoration proves complete recoverability
items.assessmentText: State: partial (reviewed 2026-09-11). The previously missing apply path now restores transferred backup data into fresh browser storage and verifies the original source SHA-256. Code: src/studio/workspaceRestoreStorage.ts. Proof: proof/growth/2026-09-11-restore/README.md. Remaining: clean-machine and native disaster drills with complete project context; a fresh browser context is not a clean machine.

items.name: Observability without secrets
items.acceptance: Error reports omit keys, private prompts and unauthorized documents
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Keys are read only in server modules and never appear in responses, failures or browser code, and evidence bundles are reviewed before archiving (`src/lib/pricingResearch.server.ts`). Remaining: there is no error reporting pipeline to audit for private prompts or unauthorised documents.

items.name: Performance and resource limits
items.acceptance: Oversized files fail safely without freezing or partial writes
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). Oversized and malformed inputs fail safely rather than corrupting state: workbook import is bounded against zip expansion, backup capture is capped, the CAD bridge enforces a size limit with cancellation, and a failed write preserves the previously stored bytes. Remaining: no freeze or partial-write behaviour has been measured under a deliberate resource-exhaustion test.

items.name: Rollback and forward compatibility
items.acceptance: Failed upgrade can recover last confirmed data revision
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). A newer stored revision is never silently overwritten and an unsupported schema fails closed with the original bytes intact, so the last confirmed data revision survives a refused change (`src/studio/persistence.ts`, `store.ts`). Remaining: there is no application upgrade path, so upgrade rollback is untested.

items.name: Support and incident handling
items.acceptance: Reproducible ticket links diagnostics, affected build and recovery
items.assessmentText: State: gap (assessed 2026-09-10). There is no incident or ticket handling linking diagnostics to an affected build.

items.name: Proof expiry after changes
items.acceptance: Dependency changes reopen affected completed acceptance rows
items.assessmentText: State: verified (assessed 2026-09-10). Stated as a governing rule of this register and applied in practice: a dependency change reopens its acceptance, superseded builds are marked superseded rather than deleted, and on 2026-09-10 every row was re-assessed against shipping code with stale claims corrected. Earlier candidate builds remain recorded as superseded with their failures preserved.

items.name: Release notes and capability contract
items.acceptance: Users see delivered limits and verified platform support
items.assessmentText: State: partial (assessed 2026-09-10). The verified build record states what the build delivers, its digests, and its known limits including the eight-step assistant pause, web-only rendering and the untested two-window native case (LATEST-VERIFIED-BUILD.md). Remaining: this is a repository record rather than release notes visible to a user inside the application.
